newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court dismisses Guerin action for damages against Commission.
newsitem.headline: Court dismisses Guerin action for damages against Commission.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance dismissed on Tuesday a claim that the European Commission's failure to investigate car manufacturer Nissan's distribution practices resulted in damages to a French car dealer.

Nissan France terminated an agreement with Guerin Automobiles, now in receivership, in 1992. Guerin wanted the Commission to say the termination violated competition rules, but the Commission did not reply to Guerin's complaints.
The court, in the first case brought by Guerin against the Commission (T-195/95), dismissed as inadmissible claims the Commission failed to act.

In this second case, the court looked at the admissibility of damage claims. Although the Commission argued a case for damages could not be made where the court had already dismissed the underlying claim, the court relied on its rules of procedure governing initial applications to find inadmissibility.
"In order to ensure legal certainty...if an action is to be admissible the essential facts and law on which it is based must be apparent from the text of the application itself..." the court said.
The court found Guerin failed to establish with sufficient "clarity and precision" a causal link between damages sought and the Commission's failure to act, in its original application.
Commission of the European Communities, defendant
action for damages based on the alleged failure of the Commission to act, in so far as its failure to take a decision on a complaint submitted by the applicant has caused the latter damage
The European Court of First Instance hereby
1. Dismisses the claims for compensation as inadmissible;
2. Orders the applicant to pay the costs, including those relating to the proceedings concerning the claim for a declaration of failure to act.
